entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider.trackAll(Map) opened unrelated baselines per entry.
entries.after: The concrete default class accepts one ordered target batch through begin.
entries.replacement: Use TrackingExecutor.execute with an ordered Target list.
entries.reason: Independent concrete calls reset phase budgets and lose batch ordering.

entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider.trackDeep(...,TrackingOptions) admitted a second options owner.
entries.after: The concrete default class consumes validated CompareOptions through begin.
entries.replacement: Map TrackingOptions once, then call TrackingExecutor.
entries.reason: The default provider cannot choose depth outside the active runtime policy.

entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider.recordChange(...) accepted arbitrary manual values.
entries.after: The concrete default class only captures canonical comparison results.
entries.replacement: Publish application events outside the comparison provider.
entries.reason: Manual values bypass bounded result, masking, and batch ownership contracts.

entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider.clearTracking(String) guessed cleanup ownership from a session name.
entries.after: The concrete default class releases resources only through batch close.
entries.replacement: Close the returned TrackingBatchScope.
entries.reason: A string session cannot safely select request-local baseline resources.

entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider.withTracked(...) directly owned and could retry a business action.
entries.after: Only final TrackingExecutor sequences the action.
entries.replacement: Use TrackingExecutor.withTracked or execute.
entries.reason: Leaving the concrete wrapper would preserve the duplicate-action path after removing it from the SPI.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.getForcedObjectType() exposed the removed ObjectType semantic override.
entries.after: TrackingOptions derives all semantics from immutable CompareOptions.
entries.replacement: Declare Entity or ValueObject descriptors and configure ComparePolicy.
entries.reason: The return type and its mutable per-call override were retired with the canonical descriptor model.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.getForcedStrategy() exposed the removed ValueObjectCompareStrategy override.
entries.after: TrackingOptions cannot select a per-call comparison strategy.
entries.replacement: Register typed strategy extensions when building CompareRuntime.
entries.reason: The return type and string-like routing owner no longer exist in the immutable runtime.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.isTypeAwareEnabled() exposed a per-request semantic mode flag.
entries.after: Type identity is fixed by the canonical runtime and descriptors.
entries.replacement: Use ComparePolicy and descriptor annotations.
entries.reason: A request flag cannot redefine the runtime equality domain.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.Builder.enableTypeAware() enabled a second type semantics path.
entries.after: The compatibility builder does not own type identity.
entries.replacement: Use canonical descriptors and ComparePolicy.
entries.reason: The no-arg toggle depended on a retired mode and could drift from runtime policy.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.Builder.enableTypeAware(boolean) mutated request-local type semantics.
entries.after: The compatibility builder cannot enable or disable canonical type identity.
entries.replacement: Use canonical descriptors and ComparePolicy.
entries.reason: A boolean request switch cannot safely override the frozen equality domain.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.Builder.forceObjectType(ObjectType) forced a removed per-call object classification.
entries.after: Object classification comes only from canonical descriptors.
entries.replacement: Use Entity or ValueObject annotations and ComparePolicy.
entries.reason: The parameter type was retired and restoring it would recreate a second classification owner.

entries.before: TrackingOptions.Builder.forceStrategy(ValueObjectCompareStrategy) selected a removed per-call strategy.
entries.after: Strategy selection is frozen in CompareRuntime.
entries.replacement: Register typed extensions through CompareRuntime.Builder.
entries.reason: The parameter type was retired and restoring it would recreate mutable strategy routing.

entries.before: TrackingProvider implementations were not required to create a typed batch scope.
entries.after: Every implementation must provide begin(List<Target>,CompareOptions).
entries.replacement: Implement begin by returning one lexical TrackingBatchScope and keep business action sequencing in TrackingExecutor.
entries.reason: Adding an abstract interface method intentionally breaks existing provider implementations so all providers obey the explicit batch lifecycle.

entries.before: TfiTrack published a second declarative tracking annotation.
entries.after: TfiTask is the only declarative tracking annotation.
entries.replacement: Use Core @TfiTask(deepTracking=true) or explicit TrackingExecutor.
entries.reason: The annotation had no production reader and activating it would create an ambiguous second advice path.

entries.before: TfiTrack.condition() advertised an unused SpEL activation condition.
entries.after: Tracking activation uses TfiTask condition at the Flow-owned advice.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask.condition().
entries.reason: An unread condition member suggested behavior that never existed.

entries.before: TfiTrack.depth() exposed a disconnected traversal depth.
entries.after: TfiTask maxDepth maps to canonical CompareOptions.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask.maxDepth() or explicit CompareOptions.
entries.reason: A second depth member could diverge from the runtime policy ceiling.

entries.before: TfiTrack.excludes() advertised unread field patterns.
entries.after: TfiTask excludeFields compiles to typed path rules.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask.excludeFields() or ComparePolicy path rules.
entries.reason: Unread string patterns formed a false configuration surface.

entries.before: TfiTrack.includes() advertised unread field patterns.
entries.after: TfiTask includeFields compiles to typed path rules.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask.includeFields() or ComparePolicy path rules.
entries.reason: Unread string patterns formed a false configuration surface.

entries.before: TfiTrack.maskSensitive() implied a per-annotation masking switch.
entries.after: Declarative publication cannot disable canonical safe masking.
entries.replacement: Use the canonical projection masking policy.
entries.reason: A local boolean must not bypass the single masking boundary.

entries.before: TfiTrack.objects() advertised SpEL-selected tracking targets.
entries.after: Complex method arguments become ordinal targets at the Flow hook.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask(deepTracking=true) or explicit TrackingExecutor targets.
entries.reason: SpEL target selection would create a second naming and selection owner.

entries.before: TfiTrack.trackNested() exposed a second traversal toggle.
entries.after: Canonical CompareOptions depth and path rules define traversal.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask.maxDepth() or explicit CompareOptions.
entries.reason: The unread toggle had no stable relation to comparison depth.

entries.before: TfiTrack.value() aliased the unused objects member.
entries.after: Declarative target selection follows one ordinal argument rule.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask(deepTracking=true) or explicit TrackingExecutor targets.
entries.reason: A second unused alias increased ambiguity without a reader.

entries.before: TfiDeepTrackingAspect exposed a second TfiTask advice owner.
entries.after: Only the Flow starter aspect owns TfiTask advice.
entries.replacement: Provide at most one TfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate bean.
entries.reason: Two aspects could duplicate action wrapping, sampling, and lifecycle decisions.

entries.before: TfiDeepTrackingAspect had a public default constructor.
entries.after: Deep tracking is composed through Spring's single delegate bean.
entries.replacement: Use DeepTrackingAutoConfiguration or construct DefaultTfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate with a provider.
entries.reason: Direct aspect construction bypassed the single-owner auto-configuration boundary.

entries.before: TfiDeepTrackingAspect accepted a ChangeConsoleExporter constructor dependency.
entries.after: Tracking results stay in the typed executor path before safe publication.
entries.replacement: Use DefaultTfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate with a TrackingProvider.
entries.reason: Exporter injection coupled advice sequencing to the retired output path.

entries.before: TfiDeepTrackingAspect.around(...) wrapped TfiTask independently of Flow sampling and stage activation.
entries.after: Flow invokes one optional delegate only inside its active stage.
entries.replacement: Implement TfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate.execute(...).
entries.reason: The public advice method preserved a second executable business path.

entries.before: DeepTrackingAutoConfiguration.tfiDeepTrackingAspect() registered the retired second advice.
entries.after: DeepTrackingAutoConfiguration registers one provider and one delegate.
entries.replacement: Use tfiTaskTrackingProvider() and tfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate(...).
entries.reason: Keeping the old bean method would make both advice paths appear supported.

entries.before: ChangeTracker exposed process-local ThreadLocal baselines and implicit global cleanup.
entries.after: Tracking state exists only inside an explicit lexical TrackingBatchScope.
entries.replacement: Use TrackingExecutor.execute or withTracked.
entries.reason: An implicit ThreadLocal owner made lifecycle, cleanup, and result ownership depend on call order.

entries.before: ChangeTracker.TrackingException represented failures from the retired implicit tracker.
entries.after: Typed input failures and canonical CompareResult problems describe explicit execution failures.
entries.replacement: Use CompareInputException or inspect TrackingExecutor results.
entries.reason: Keeping an exception owned by a removed lifecycle would imply the old execution path remained supported.

entries.before: SessionAwareChangeTracker published a static process-wide session history store.
entries.after: Compare publishes no global or session history owner.
entries.replacement: Persist explicit TrackingExecutor.Execution results in an application-owned sink when history is required.
entries.reason: The static map was not guaranteed to receive canonical tracking results and therefore could not be an operational fact source.

entries.before: SessionMetadata exposed counters derived from the retired static session map.
entries.after: No Compare API claims session age, activity, or global change counts.
entries.replacement: Define application-owned history metadata beside the application-owned sink.
entries.reason: Metadata without a canonical writer makes unknown state look authoritative.

entries.before: TfiCompareHealthIndicator derived health from the non-canonical session store.
entries.after: Ops health consumes JVM and Core Context facts only.
entries.replacement: Use tfi-ops-spring TfiHealthCalculator or the read-only endpoints.
entries.reason: A health indicator must not report UP from absent or unwritten tracking history.

entries.before: TfiCompareHealthAutoConfiguration installed Compare-owned pseudo-health.
entries.after: Compare no longer auto-configures an Actuator health owner.
entries.replacement: Use tfi-ops-spring diagnostics backed by ContextMetrics.
entries.reason: Operational endpoints belong to Ops and must consume facts with a real runtime owner.

entries.before: CleanupConfiguration scheduled cleanup of the retired static session history.
entries.after: No Compare scheduler mutates session or global tracking state.
entries.replacement: Close each TrackingBatchScope lexically; application history sinks own their retention.
entries.reason: A scheduler cannot repair ownership for state that the canonical path never writes.

entries.before: ActuatorConfiguration advertised an empty Compare-owned management integration.
entries.after: Compare auto-configuration publishes no empty Actuator surface.
entries.replacement: Use the concrete read-only endpoints from tfi-ops-spring.
entries.reason: An empty conditional configuration preserves a false ownership boundary and adds no runtime capability.

entries.before: Spring configuration metadata advertised lossy List routing, Map candidate, and PerfGuard settings.
entries.after: The metadata no longer publishes collection algorithm or sampling fallback settings.
entries.replacement: Use ComparePolicy and CompareOptions bounded limits.
entries.reason: Published metadata is a consumer contract and must not advertise removed semantic owners.

entries.before: Ops Spring metadata advertised access-log, session warning, tracked-object, change-history, and value limits without runtime readers.
entries.after: Ops metadata publishes only configuration consumed by current metrics, masking, cache, Context health, and endpoint activation paths.
entries.replacement: Use ContextMetrics for current process diagnostics and application-owned storage for explicit tracking history.
entries.reason: Metadata is a public capability claim and cannot preserve controls for state or helpers removed from the runtime.

entries.before: tfi.compare.auto-route.* could switch ordinary List strategy by content or size.
entries.after: No automatic collection routing keys are bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use the frozen CompareRuntime strategy table.
entries.reason: Environment configuration must not change facts for identical List inputs.

entries.before: tfi.diff.perf.algo.* configured LCS, edit-distance, and rename routes.
entries.after: No performance algorithm configuration family is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use ordered-index List comparison and exact Map keys.
entries.reason: Algorithm choice is semantic policy, not a performance tuning option.

entries.before: tfi.diff.perf.degradation-strategy selected a free-form fallback algorithm.
entries.after: No fallback strategy key is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use bounded limits and inspect typed partial completion.
entries.reason: A string fallback selector can silently change collection truth.

entries.before: tfi.change-tracking.degradation.list-size-threshold switched List execution at a size boundary.
entries.after: No semantic List size threshold is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use CompareOptions maxElements for a visible partial boundary.
entries.reason: List meaning must remain stable across input sizes.

entries.before: tfi.change-tracking.degradation.k-pairs-threshold enabled sampling fallback.
entries.after: No K-pairs threshold is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use the shared ledger and typed partial completion.
entries.reason: Sampling may omit changes and cannot represent complete comparison.

entries.before: tfi.change-tracking.degradation.max-candidates bounded heuristic Map rename pairing.
entries.after: No Map candidate threshold is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use exact canonical Map key pairing.
entries.reason: Candidate limits have no place after rename inference is removed.

entries.before: tfi.perf-guard.* configured runtime collection fallback behavior.
entries.after: No PerfGuard configuration family is bound or published.
entries.replacement: Use ComparePolicy and immutable CompareOptions limits.
entries.reason: Operational fallback configuration was a second semantic owner.

entries.before: tfi.actuator.access-log.* configured an endpoint-local map that had no operational reader.
entries.after: The read-only endpoint performs no unused access-log mutation and publishes no access-log controls.
entries.replacement: Use platform access logs when request auditing is required.
entries.reason: A GET diagnostics path must not retain process-local state solely for an unreachable private counter.

entries.before: tfi.health.max-sessions-warning and tfi.limits.* advertised limits for global tracking history with no canonical writer.
entries.after: Ops health and stats consume only JVM and ContextMetrics facts with active runtime owners.
entries.replacement: Bound explicit TrackingExecutor calls with ComparePolicy and retain history in an application-owned sink.
entries.reason: Unused limits make unknown session and change state look like a supported operational capability.

entries.before: Map comparison treated absent and present-null as the same lookup result.
entries.after: Presence and value are evaluated separately, including null keys and values.
entries.replacement: Consume exact REMOVE, ADD, MODIFY, and NULLNESS facts.
entries.reason: Map.get alone cannot distinguish a missing key from a present null value.

entries.before: Similar Map values could trigger a heuristic key rename update.
entries.after: Different keys always produce independent REMOVE and ADD facts.
entries.replacement: Model domain rename intent explicitly outside generic Map comparison.
entries.reason: Generic comparison has no evidence that two different keys represent one identity.

entries.before: Ordinary Lists could route through LCS, edit-distance, AsSet, or sampled plans.
entries.after: Ordinary Lists compare each addressable index in order at every size.
entries.replacement: Pass Set explicitly for unordered semantics; entity pairing remains a separate strategy.
entries.reason: One List type must have one deterministic semantic plan.

entries.before: Equal truncated or summary representations could short-circuit element comparison as equal.
entries.after: Summary representation is diagnostic only and cannot prove element equality.
entries.replacement: Inspect outcome, completion, and typed limitations together.
entries.reason: Two distinct values may share the same bounded display prefix or summary.

entries.before: Collection work beyond a threshold could be sampled while comparison appeared complete.
entries.after: Exhausting the shared element budget stops before unobserved facts and publishes PARTIAL.
entries.replacement: Increase explicit limits or handle typed partial completion.
entries.reason: Unobserved elements cannot support a complete equality claim.

entries.before: Legacy deep snapshot modes could replace large Collection, Map, or array elements with summaries or truncation markers.
entries.after: Legacy snapshot capture retains addressable container elements instead of substituting summary truth.
entries.replacement: Use explicit comparison budgets for bounded result truth; summaries remain presentation diagnostics.
entries.reason: A snapshot used as comparison input cannot silently discard changed tail elements.

entries.before: Entity ID or non-scalar equals could terminate comparison after candidate matching.
entries.after: Identity only pairs candidates; paired List, Set, and Map values continue through field comparison.
entries.replacement: Use typed comparators only for an explicitly registered terminal equality rule.
entries.reason: Business identity equality does not prove that mutable entity content is equal.

entries.before: A keyed List reorder could publish only movement or only an index-based modification.
entries.after: Unique entity keys publish physical MOVE facts and retain field changes on the stable entity path.
entries.replacement: Consume MOVE and MODIFY as independent facts for the same keyed entity.
entries.reason: Position and content are independent dimensions and neither may overwrite the other.

entries.before: Set classification could depend on the first member and iteration order.
entries.after: Null, scalar, entity, and complex members are classified independently with deterministic typed facts.
entries.replacement: Consume SetMemberSegment or EntityKeySegment paths according to each member kind.
entries.reason: A heterogeneous Set has no representative first element and iteration order is not semantic evidence.

entries.before: Unmarked complex Set members could be collapsed by business equals or bounded display text.
entries.after: Complete canonical typed snapshots determine complex Set member grouping.
entries.replacement: Declare Entity with an exact key when cross-version identity pairing is required.
entries.reason: Neither non-scalar equals nor display summaries can prove full member content equality.

entries.before: Duplicate entity keys could use first-wins pairing and overwrite or hide members.
entries.after: Duplicate identity publishes W2201 while independently resolvable sibling changes remain visible.
entries.replacement: Resolve duplicate domain identity before relying on complete comparison.
entries.reason: The kernel cannot infer a deterministic one-to-one relation among duplicate keys.

entries.before: An inaccessible or non-scalar entity key could fall back to physical List index pairing.
entries.after: Unresolved entity identity publishes W2201 and no synthetic element change.
entries.replacement: Use an accessible closed-scalar @Key or handle PARTIAL completion.
entries.reason: Physical position cannot substitute for declared business identity without guessing.

entries.before: A field marked both @Key and @DiffIgnore could still participate in entity pairing.
entries.after: The conflicting descriptor publishes a typed problem before candidate pairing.
entries.replacement: Remove one conflicting annotation so identity and the comparison field domain agree.
entries.reason: An ignored field cannot simultaneously define cross-container identity without violating the declared equality domain.

entries.before: DefaultTrackingProvider could execute a failing business action twice and swallow its exception.
entries.after: TrackingExecutor invokes action exactly once and propagates the same business exception instance.
entries.replacement: Route all tracking actions through final TrackingExecutor.
entries.reason: Infrastructure failure must never alter business action cardinality or identity.

entries.before: TrackingOptions accepted depth and time budgets beyond the canonical Compare runtime limits.
entries.after: Legacy resource requests are clamped to the immutable ComparePolicy boundary.
entries.replacement: Inspect TrackingOptions.toCompareOptions() and configure a deliberate ComparePolicy before runtime construction.
entries.reason: A compatibility adapter cannot expand the active runtime safety limits.

entries.before: TrackingOptions retained independent depth, collection, comparison, monitoring, and summary state.
entries.after: TrackingOptions instances retain only one immutable CompareOptions value; unsupported legacy switches are stateless compatibility calls.
entries.replacement: Use ComparePolicy and CompareOptions as the only tracking configuration owner.
entries.reason: Duplicated option state could drift from the provider runtime and select a second execution graph.

entries.before: TrackingOptions retained and re-exposed raw include and exclude field sets.
entries.after: Legacy field selectors compile once as typed PROPERTY rules and raw selector text is not retained by TrackingOptions.
entries.replacement: Read canonical results rather than round-tripping raw selector configuration.
entries.reason: One-way compatibility mapping must not create a second raw path-rule owner or leak selectors through diagnostics.

entries.before: TFI.withTracked(..., fields) selected a per-call field subset outside the provider runtime.
entries.after: The static facade preserves the source signature but legacy fields do not change the resolved provider's equality domain.
entries.replacement: Configure typed path rules in ComparePolicy when constructing the provider runtime, or call TrackingExecutor directly.
entries.reason: Applying raw per-call fields would create a second policy graph and make comparison truth depend on the facade path.

entries.before: TfiTrack Javadoc described SpEL tracking although no production reader existed.
entries.after: The no-op annotation and its examples are removed.
entries.replacement: Use TfiTask(deepTracking=true) or explicit TrackingExecutor.
entries.reason: Documentation must not imply a second declarative path that the runtime does not execute.

entries.before: Compare's aspect independently wrapped TfiTask actions and used thread-local ChangeTracker publication.
entries.after: Flow owns the sole advice and invokes one explicit delegate inside the active stage.
entries.replacement: Use the TfiTaskDeepTrackingDelegate hook.
entries.reason: One action path prevents duplicate sampling, execution, cleanup, and publication semantics.

entries.before: TfiTask SUMMARY could select a separate lossy collection summary path.
entries.after: SUMMARY maps to the same complete member comparison as ELEMENT.
entries.replacement: Use ELEMENT for explicit intent; SUMMARY remains a one-way migration token.
entries.reason: A second collection truth domain would make identical inputs depend on a legacy label.

entries.before: TfiTask IGNORE could hide the entire container.
entries.after: IGNORE excludes member values but preserves container nullness, kind, and exact size.
entries.replacement: Use IGNORE only when structural container facts remain part of equality.
entries.reason: Ignoring the container itself would erase observable structural changes.

entries.before: Implicit tracker calls accumulated baselines in ThreadLocal state until a later stop or clear call.
entries.after: Each explicit TrackingExecutor call owns capture and close inside one lexical boundary.
entries.replacement: Wrap the business action with TrackingExecutor.execute or TFI.withTracked.
entries.reason: Lexical ownership removes call-order-dependent cleanup and cross-request retention.

entries.before: Ops reported session and change zero values from a store without a canonical writer.

entries.replacement: Use the read-only Context diagnostics or persist explicit tracking results in an application sink.
entries.reason: Unknown history must not be represented as an authoritative zero.

entries.before: Actuator endpoints exposed session cleanup and pseudo runtime update operations.
entries.after: Tracking-related Ops endpoints are read-only and expose only overview, config, and Context stats.
entries.replacement: Change startup configuration outside the endpoint and close explicit scopes in application code.
entries.reason: A management operation cannot mutate state when no runtime owner exists for that state.

entries.before: SecureTfiEndpoint retained an unused Micrometer dependency and a write-only access log; orphan session helpers implied a removed endpoint still existed.
entries.after: The endpoint depends only on facts it reads, and obsolete session/access helper types are absent.
entries.replacement: Use the canonical metrics endpoint for Micrometer data and platform access logs for request auditing.
entries.reason: Dead dependencies and helpers preserve ambiguous ownership even when no route can consume their state.

entries.before: Invalid or null options could be defaulted after entering a provider or action.
entries.after: Options are validated against the active policy before comparison side effects.
entries.replacement: Use the no-options overload or pass CompareOptions built for the active policy.
entries.reason: Input rejection must be deterministic and must not execute comparison work first.

entries.before: Service, provider and facade could each construct a default comparison graph.
entries.after: All pure-Java default entry points share CompareRuntime.defaults().
entries.replacement: Construct custom graphs only with CompareRuntime.Builder.
entries.reason: A single frozen graph prevents entry-point-specific defaults and half-updated registries.

entries.before: Registered property comparators could be stored without affecting engine execution.
entries.after: Exact declared-field comparators participate in comparison and failures do not fall back.
entries.replacement: Register exact PropertySelector comparators through CompareRuntime.Builder.
entries.reason: An extension registration is a frozen semantic choice, not advisory metadata.

entries.before: List execution could read Spring routing, PerfGuard and degradation state and switch algorithms at runtime.
entries.after: List routing is determined only by the frozen strategy table and input type.
entries.replacement: Choose limits in ComparePolicy and extensions in CompareRuntime.Builder.
entries.reason: Runtime fallback changes semantics across identical requests and creates a second policy owner.

entries.before: JSON, Map, Markdown, and Console interpreted independent field trees, statistics, timestamps, and value representations.
entries.after: All retained output paths consume schema tfi.compare.change version 1 with one ordered projection tree and tagged ValueSnapshot wire.
entries.replacement: Build CompareProjection with CompareProjectionFactory and encode the prebuilt projection.
entries.reason: Independent formatter trees drift in field meaning, ordering, and omission semantics.

entries.before: Mutable formatter flags and system properties could weaken masking while each formatter inspected raw values independently.
entries.after: MaskingPolicy applies an immutable safe floor before formatting; mutable legacy flags cannot publish sensitive values.
entries.replacement: Use MaskingPolicy.explicitlyIncludeSensitiveValues() only for an audited single projection call.
entries.reason: A global or formatter-local opt-out can leak exact scalar, metadata, key, or path facts across output formats.

entries.before: TfiListDiff.render accepted a weak Object style.
entries.after: TfiListDiff exposes one canonical Markdown render entry.
entries.replacement: Call TfiListDiff.render(CompareResult).
entries.reason: Weak style parsing recreated output defaults at the facade.

entries.before: TfiListDiffFacade.render accepted a weak Object style.

entries.reason: A weak style value allowed entry-specific output policy.

entries.before: ExporterConfiguration required TfiConfig to select one configured format.
entries.after: Stateless target formatters are assembled without an output selector.

entries.reason: A singleton format choice conflicted with the typed per-call boundary.

entries.before: ExporterConfiguration published mutable ChangeExporter.ExportConfig.
entries.after: No mutable formatter configuration bean is published.

entries.reason: A mutable bean could change masking and schema behavior after construction.

entries.before: ChangeTracking construction included the retired Export component.

entries.before: ChangeTracking.export exposed unread output configuration.

entries.reason: Publishing an unread record component is a false runtime contract.

entries.before: Diff construction included the unused outputMode component.

entries.replacement: Use RenderOptions after projection construction.
entries.reason: Diff policy must not own presentation mode.

entries.before: Diff.outputMode exposed presentation state from comparison configuration.
entries.after: Diff exposes no output mode.

entries.reason: Comparison semantics and diagnostic layout require separate owners.

entries.before: TfiConfig.ChangeTracking.Export modeled mutable-style output flags.

entries.reason: The type had no production reader and implied unsafe controls.

entries.before: ChangeConsoleExporter formatted raw ChangeRecord lists.

entries.before: ChangeConsoleExporter accepted raw records and mutable ExportConfig.

entries.before: ChangeExporter defined a raw-list and mutable-config formatter contract.
entries.after: Each target formatter accepts typed CompareProjection.
entries.replacement: Use ChangeJsonExporter, ChangeMapExporter, MarkdownRenderer, or ChangeConsoleExporter.

entries.before: ChangeExporter.ExportConfig allowed mutable masking and layout flags.

entries.reason: One mutable object mixed security, schema, and presentation concerns.

entries.before: ChangeJsonExporter accepted an ExportMode constructor selector.

entries.before: ChangeJsonExporter accepted raw records and mutable ExportConfig.

entries.reason: Multiple implicit JSON modes defeat stable machine consumption.

entries.before: ChangeMapExporter exposed a public instance constructor for static legacy helpers.

entries.reason: Instances had no state or extension contract.

entries.before: ChangeMapExporter exported raw ChangeRecord lists.

entries.before: ChangeMapExporter accepted raw records and mutable ExportConfig.

entries.before: ChangeXmlExporter published a second nested machine schema.
